units.zh: 永王存霸，武皇子，莊宗第二弟，同光三年封。
units.en: Prince Yong Cunba, a son of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong's second younger brother, received his princely title in Tongguang 3.
units.literal: Prince Yong Cunba, son of the Martial Emperor, Emperor Zhuangzong's second younger brother, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

units.zh: 莊宗敗，為軍卒所殺。
units.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, he was killed by common soldiers.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, he was killed by soldiers.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：存霸曆昭義、天平、河中三軍節度使，居京師食俸祿而已。
units.en: (The Ouyang History records that Cunba had served in turn as military commissioner of the Zhao-Yi, Tianping, and Hezhong circuits, living in the capital on stipend alone.
units.literal: (The Ouyang History states: Cunba successively held the posts of military commissioner of the Zhao-Yi, Tianping, and Hezhong armies, residing in the capital and drawing salary only.

units.zh: 趙在禮反，乃遣存霸於河中，莊宗再幸汜水，徙存霸北京留守。
units.en: When Zhao Zaili rose in revolt, Cunba was dispatched to Hezhong. Zhuangzong returned to Si River a second time and reassigned Cunba as Protector of the Northern Capital.
units.literal: When Zhao Zaili rebelled, Cunba was sent to Hezhong; Emperor Zhuangzong again visited Si River and transferred Cunba to be Northern Capital Protector.

units.zh: 《通鑒》云：李紹榮欲奔河中就永王存霸，從兵稍散，存霸亦率眾千人棄鎮奔晉陽。
units.en: The Comprehensive Mirror adds that Li Shaorong meant to flee to Hezhong to reach Prince Yong Cunba, but his followers slowly melted away, and Cunba too abandoned his command with a thousand men and fled to Jinyang.
units.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror states: Li Shaorong wished to flee to Hezhong to join Prince Yong Cunba; his followers gradually dispersed, and Cunba also led a thousand men in abandoning his post and fleeing to Jinyang.

units.zh: 又云：存霸至晉陽，從兵逃散俱盡，存霸削髮僧服謁李彥超：「願為山僧，幸垂庇護。」
units.en: The text goes on to say that by the time Cunba reached Jinyang every one of his followers had deserted him. He shaved his head, put on monastic robes, and visited Li Yanchao, saying, "I wish only to be a mountain monk; please grant me your protection."
units.literal: It also states: When Cunba reached Jinyang his followers had all fled and scattered. Cunba shaved his head, donned monk's robes, and called on Li Yanchao: "I wish to be a mountain monk; I beg your protection."

units.zh: 軍士爭欲殺之，彥超曰：「六相公來，當奏取進止。」
units.en: The troops clamored to kill him, but Li Yanchao said, "The Sixth Lord has arrived; I must submit a report and await instructions."
units.literal: The soldiers competed to kill him. Li Yanchao said: "The Sixth Lord has come; I should memorialize and await orders."

units.zh: 軍士不聽，殺之於府門之碑下。）〉
units.en: The soldiers refused to wait and killed him at the stele before the prefectural gate.)〉
units.literal: The soldiers would not listen and killed him below the stele at the government gate.)〉

units.zh: 邕王存美，武皇子，莊宗第三弟，同光三年封。
units.en: Prince of Yong Cunmei, a son of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong's third younger brother, received his title in Tongguang 3.
units.literal: Prince Yong Cunmei, son of the Martial Emperor, Emperor Zhuangzong's third younger brother, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

units.zh: 莊宗敗，不知所終。
units.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, his fate was never learned.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, his end was unknown.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：存美以病風偏枯得免，居於晉陽。）〉
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror notes that Cunmei was spared because wind sickness had left him half-paralyzed, and he remained at Jinyang.)〉
units.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: Cunmei, because he suffered hemiplegia from wind disease, was spared and lived at Jinyang.)〉

units.zh: 薛王存禮，武皇子，同光三年封。
units.en: Prince Xue Cunli, a son of the Martial Emperor, was enfeoffed in Tongguang 3.
units.literal: Prince Xue Cunli, son of the Martial Emperor, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

units.zh: 莊宗敗，不知所終。
units.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, his fate was never learned.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, his end was unknown.

units.zh: 申王存渥，莊宗第四弟，
units.en: Prince Shen Cunwo, Zhuangzong's fourth younger brother,
units.literal: Prince Shen Cunwo, Emperor Zhuangzong's fourth younger brother,

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》，存渥與存霸、存紀皆莊宗同母弟。）〉
units.en: (The Ouyang History adds that Cunwo, like Cunba and Cunji, was Zhuangzong's uterine younger brother.)〉
units.literal: (The Ouyang History [notes]: Cunwo, together with Cunba and Cunji, were all Emperor Zhuangzong's younger brothers by the same mother.)〉

units.zh: 同光三年封。
units.en: He received his princely title in Tongguang 3.
units.literal: was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

units.zh: 莊宗敗，與劉皇后同奔太原，為部下所殺。
units.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, he fled toward Taiyuan with Empress Liu and was killed by his own followers.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, he fled to Taiyuan together with Empress Liu and was killed by his subordinates.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：存渥至晉陽，李彥超不納，走至風穀，為其下所殺。）〉
units.en: (According to the Comprehensive Mirror, Cunwo reached Jinyang but Li Yanchao refused him entry; fleeing as far as Feng Valley, he was killed by his own party.)〉
units.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: When Cunwo reached Jinyang, Li Yanchao would not admit him; he fled to Feng Valley and was killed by his men.)〉

units.zh: 睦王存乂，莊宗第五弟，同光三所封。
units.en: Prince Mu Cunyi, Zhuangzong's fifth younger brother, was enfeoffed in Tongguang 3.
units.literal: Prince Mu Cunyi, Emperor Zhuangzong's fifth younger brother, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

units.zh: 〈（案，以下原闕。）〉
units.en: (Note: the original text below this point is missing.)〉
units.literal: (Examination shows the original text is missing below.)〉

units.zh: 曆鄜州節度使，後以郭崇韜婿為莊宗所殺。
units.en: He had served as military commissioner of Fuzhou and was later executed by Zhuangzong for being Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.
units.literal: He successively served as military commissioner of Fuzhou and was later killed by Emperor Zhuangzong because he was Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：莊宗異母弟存乂，以郭崇韜女婿伏誅。
units.en: (Beimeng Suoyan records that Cunyi, Zhuangzong's half-brother, was put to death for being married to Guo Chongtao's daughter.
units.literal: (Beimeng Suoyan states: Cunyi, Emperor Zhuangzong's younger brother by a different mother, was executed because he was Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.

units.zh: 先是，郭崇韜既誅之後，朝野駭惋，議論紛然。
units.en: After Guo Chongtao's execution, the court and the streets alike were shaken with horror and regret, and debate raged on every side.
units.literal: Earlier, after Guo Chongtao had been executed, court and commoners alike were shaken and aggrieved, and opinion was in uproar.

units.zh: 莊宗令閹人察訪外事，言存乂於諸將坐上訴郭氏之無罪，其言怨望。
units.en: Zhuangzong sent eunuchs to spy on affairs beyond the palace, and they reported that seated among the generals Cunyi had argued for the Guo family's innocence in tones full of resentment.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong ordered eunuchs to investigate external affairs, and they reported that at a gathering of generals Cunyi, seated among them, pleaded Guo's innocence, speaking with resentment.

units.zh: 又於妖術人楊千郎家飲酒聚會，攘臂而泣。
units.en: He had also been seen drinking with friends at the home of the wonder-worker Yang Qianlang, where he rolled up his sleeves and wept aloud.
units.literal: Furthermore, at drinking gatherings at the house of the sorcerer Yang Qianlang he rolled up his sleeves and wept.

units.zh: 楊千郎者，魏州賤民，自言得墨子術於婦翁，能役使陰物，帽下召食物果實之類。
units.en: Yang Qianlang was a common man of Weizhou who claimed to have learned Mozi's techniques from his father-in-law and could command spirits of the yin realm: food, fruit, and other provisions would appear from under his cap.
units.literal: Yang Qianlang was a lowly man of Weizhou who claimed to have received Mozi's arts from his wife's father and could command yin spirits; beneath his hat he could summon food and fruit and the like.

units.zh: 又蒱爪博必勝，人有拳握之物，以法必取。
units.en: In finger-wrestling and dice games he never lost, and whatever a man clenched in his fist, Yang could always draw forth by his arts.
units.literal: Furthermore, in finger-guessing and gambling games he was sure to win; if someone held something clenched in his fist, by his arts he was sure to take it.

units.zh: 又說煉丹乾汞，易人形，破扃鑰。
units.en: He also boasted of alchemical mastery over cinnabar and mercury, of changing a man's shape, and of opening any lock.
units.literal: He also claimed to refine cinnabar with heated mercury, change human form, and break locks.

units.zh: 貴要間神奇之，官至尚書郎，賜紫，其妻出入宮禁，承恩用事。
units.en: The great and powerful marveled at him. He rose to Gentleman of the Secretariat, was granted the purple robe, and his wife moved freely through the inner palace, enjoying imperial favor and real power.
units.literal: Among the great and influential he was regarded as miraculous; he reached the office of Gentleman of the Secretariat and was granted purple robes; his wife entered and left the palace precincts, enjoying favor and wielding influence.

units.zh: 皇弟存乂常朋淫於其家，至是與存乂並罹其禍。）〉
units.en: Prince Cunyi was a habitual reveler at Yang's house; now Yang and Cunyi alike fell victim to the same purge.)〉
units.literal: The imperial younger brother Cunyi often caroused licentiously at his house, and on this occasion together with Cunyi he fell into the calamity.)〉

units.zh: 通王存確，莊宗第六弟，雅王存紀，莊宗第七弟，同光三年封。
units.en: Prince Tong Cunque, Zhuangzong's sixth younger brother, and Prince Ya Cunji, his seventh, both received their titles in Tongguang 3.
units.literal: Prince Tong Cunque, Emperor Zhuangzong's sixth younger brother, and Prince Ya Cunji, Emperor Zhuangzong's seventh younger brother, were enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

units.zh: 莊宗敗，並為霍彥威所殺。
units.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, both were killed by Huo Yanwei.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, both were killed by Huo Yanwei.

units.zh: 〈（考《梁紀》，太祖有子廷鸞、落落；
units.en: (Cross-checking the Liang Annals shows that Taizu had sons named Tingluan and Luoluo;
units.literal: (Examining the Liang Annals, Taizu had sons Tingluan and Luoluo;

units.zh: 《盧文進傳》，莊宗又有弟存矩。
units.en: the biography of Lu Wenjin mentions another younger brother of Zhuangzong, Cunju;
units.literal: in the biography of Lu Wenjin, Emperor Zhuangzong also had a younger brother Cunju.

units.zh: 《薛史宗室傳》皆不載。）〉
units.en: yet none of these appear in the imperial-family biographies of the Xue History.)〉
units.literal: None of these are recorded in the Xue History's imperial family biographies.)〉

units.zh: 魏王繼岌，莊宗子也。
units.en: Prince Wei Jiji was a son of Zhuangzong.
units.literal: Prince Wei Jiji was Emperor Zhuangzong's son.

units.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，以繼岌充北都留守；
units.en: When Zhuangzong assumed the throne at Weizhou, he appointed Jiji Protector of the Northern Capital;
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Jiji was made Northern Capital Protector;

units.zh: 及以鎮州為北都，又命為留守。
units.en: when the seat of the Northern Capital was moved to Zhenzhou, Jiji was ordered to serve there again as Protector.
units.literal: and when Zhenzhou was made the Northern Capital, he was again ordered to serve as Protector.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：三年九月二十三日，封為魏王。）〉
units.en: (According to the Five Dynasties Institutional Essentials, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei on the twenty-third day of the ninth month of that year.)〉
units.literal: (Five Dynasties Institutional Essentials: On the twenty-third day of the ninth month of the third year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.)〉

units.zh: 三年，伐蜀，以繼岌為都統，郭崇韜為招討使。
units.en: In Tongguang 3 the court marched against Shu, with Jiji as commander-in-chief and Guo Chongtao as campaign commissioner.
units.literal: In the third year they campaigned against Shu; Jiji was made commander-in-chief and Guo Chongtao campaign commissioner.

units.zh: 十月戊寅，至鳳州，武興軍節度使王承捷以鳳、興、文、扶四州降。
units.en: On wuyin in the tenth month they reached Fengzhou, where Wang Chengjie, military commissioner of the Wuxing circuit, surrendered Feng, Xing, Wen, and Fu.
units.literal: On the wuyin day of the tenth month they reached Fengzhou; Wang Chengjie, military commissioner of Wuxing Army, surrendered the four prefectures Feng, Xing, Wen, and Fu.

units.zh: 甲申，至故鎮，康延孝收興州。
units.en: On jiashen they reached Gu Town, and Kang Yanxiao took Xingzhou.
units.literal: On the jiashen day they reached Gu Town; Kang Yanxiao recovered Xingzhou.

units.zh: 時偽蜀主王衍率親軍五萬在利州，令步騎親軍三萬逆戰於三泉，康延孝、李嚴以勁騎三千犯之，蜀軍大敗，斬首五千級，餘皆奔潰。
units.en: The Shu pretender Wang Yan was then at Lizhou with fifty thousand household troops. He sent thirty thousand foot and horse of his personal guard to meet the Tang advance at Sanquan. Kang Yanxiao and Li Yan charged with three thousand elite cavalry; the Shu force was shattered, five thousand heads were taken, and the survivors fled in disorder.
units.literal: At that time the false Shu ruler Wang Yan led fifty thousand personal troops at Lizhou and ordered thirty thousand infantry and cavalry of his personal army to meet the attack at Sanquan. Kang Yanxiao and Li Yan struck them with three thousand crack horsemen; the Shu army was utterly defeated, five thousand heads were taken, and the rest all fled in rout.

units.zh: 王衍聞其敗也，棄利州奔歸西川，斷吉柏津，浮梁而去。
units.en: Hearing of the defeat, Wang Yan abandoned Lizhou and fled west into Shu, severing the Jibo crossing and escaping over a pontoon bridge.
units.literal: When Wang Yan heard of the defeat, he abandoned Lizhou and fled back to western Shu, cutting the Jibo Ford and departing by pontoon bridge.

units.zh: 己丑，繼岌至興州，偽蜀東川節度使宋光葆以梓、潼、劍、龍、普等州來降；
units.en: On jichou Jiji reached Xingzhou, where Song Guangbao, the Dongchuan military commissioner of Shu, surrendered Zi, Tong, Jian, Long, Pu, and other prefectures;
units.literal: On the jichou day Jiji reached Xingzhou; Song Guangbao, military commissioner of eastern Shu Dongchuan, came to surrender with the prefectures Zi, Tong, Jian, Long, Pu, and others;

units.zh: 武定軍節度使王承肇以洋、蓬、壁三州符印降；
units.en: Wang Chengzhao of the Wuding circuit submitted the seals of Yang, Peng, and Bi;
units.literal: Wang Chengzhao, military commissioner of Wuding Army, surrendered with the seals of the three prefectures Yang, Peng, and Bi;

units.zh: 興元節度使王宗威以梁、開、通、渠、麟等五州符印送降；
units.en: Wang Zongwei of Xingyuan sent in the seals of Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin in submission;
units.literal: Wang Zongwei, military commissioner of Xingyuan, sent the seals of the five prefectures Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin in surrender;

units.zh: 階州王承嶽納符印；
units.en: Wang Chengyue of Jiezhou turned over his seals;
units.literal: Wang Chengyue of Jiezhou presented the seals;

units.zh: 秦州節度使王承休棄城而遁。
units.en: and Wang Chengxu of Qinzhou abandoned his city and fled.
units.literal: Wang Chengxu, military commissioner of Qinzhou, abandoned the city and fled.

units.zh: 辛丑，繼岌過利州。
units.en: On xinchou Jiji passed through Lizhou.
units.literal: On the xinchou day Jiji passed Lizhou.

units.zh: 戊申，至劍州。
units.en: On wushen they reached Jianzhou.
units.literal: On the wushen day they reached Jianzhou.

units.zh: 己酉，至綿州，王衍遣使上箋乞降。
units.en: On jiyou they reached Mianzhou, where Wang Yan sent envoys with a written plea to surrender.
units.literal: On the jiyou day they reached Mianzhou; Wang Yan sent envoys with a memorial begging to surrender.

units.zh: 丁巳，入成都。
units.en: On dingsi they entered Chengdu.
units.literal: On the dingsi day they entered Chengdu.

units.zh: 自興師出洛至定蜀，計七十五日，走丸之勢，前代所無。
units.en: From the army's departure from Luoyang to the pacification of Shu took only seventy-five days—a speed like a ball rolling downhill, without precedent in earlier times.
units.literal: From raising the army and leaving Luoyang to pacifying Shu, the total was seventy-five days—a momentum like a rolling pellet, unmatched in former ages.

units.zh: 師回，至渭南，聞莊宗敗。
units.en: On the march home the army reached Weinan and learned of Zhuangzong's defeat.
units.literal: The army returned and, reaching Weinan, heard that Emperor Zhuangzong had been defeated.

units.zh: 師徒潰散，自縊死。
units.en: His force dissolved in panic, and he hanged himself.
units.literal: The troops and followers scattered in rout, and he hanged himself.

units.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》引《王氏見聞錄》云：後唐莊宗巴子魏王繼岌伐蜀，回軍在道，而有鄴都之變。
units.en: (The Extensive Records of the Taiping, citing Wang's Records of Things Seen and Heard, relates that Zhuangzong's son Prince Wei Jiji marched against Shu and was already on the homeward road when the upheaval at Ye Capital broke out.
units.literal: (Extensive Records of the Taiping cites Wang's Records of Things Seen and Heard: Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong's son Prince Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu; the army was on the road returning when the Ye Capital upheaval occurred.

units.zh: 莊宗與劉後命內臣張漢賓齎急詔，所在催魏王歸闕。
units.en: Zhuangzong and Empress Liu dispatched the palace eunuch Zhang Hanbin with an urgent edict ordering Prince Wei to return to court at once.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong and Empress Liu ordered the inner attendant Zhang Hanbin to carry an urgent edict, urging Prince Wei to return to the capital wherever he might be.

units.zh: 張漢賓乘驛倍道急行，至興元西縣逢魏王，宣傳詔旨。
units.en: Zhang Hanbin raced by post relay at top speed, met Prince Wei at Xixian in Xingyuan, and delivered the imperial command.
units.literal: Zhang Hanbin rode the post relays at double speed and, reaching Xixian in Xingyuan, met Prince Wei and proclaimed the edict.

units.zh: 王以本軍方討漢州，康延孝相次繼來，欲候之出山，以陳凱歌，漢賓督之。
units.en: The prince's own force was still reducing Hanzhou, and Kang Yanxiao was following close behind; he wanted to wait until both columns had cleared the mountains to celebrate victory, but Hanbin pressed him onward.
units.literal: The prince, because his own army was still campaigning at Hanzhou and Kang Yanxiao was coming in succession, wished to wait for them to emerge from the mountains so as to proclaim victory; Hanbin pressed him.

units.zh: 有軍謀陳岷，比事梁，與漢賓熟，密問張曰：「天子改換，且是何人？」
units.en: A staff officer named Chen Min, who had once served Liang and knew Hanbin well, asked him in private, "The throne has changed hands—who sits on it now?"
units.literal: There was a military adviser Chen Min who had formerly served Liang and was on familiar terms with Hanbin; he secretly asked Zhang: "The Son of Heaven has been replaced—who is it now?"

units.zh: 張色莊曰：「我嘗麵奉宣詔魏王，況大軍在行，談何容易。」
units.en: Zhang's face hardened. "I received this edict in person to deliver to Prince Wei, and a great army is on the march—such talk is not to be bandied about lightly."
units.literal: Zhang's expression grew stern: "I once received the edict face to face to proclaim it to Prince Wei; moreover the great army is on the march—how can such talk be lightly made?"

units.zh: 陳岷曰：「久忝知聞，故敢諮問，兩日來有一信風，新人已即位矣，復何形跡。」
units.en: Chen Min replied, "We have known each other a long time, which is why I dare ask. For two days reliable word has been blowing this way: the new man is already enthroned. Why keep up appearances?"
units.literal: Chen Min said: "Having long enjoyed your acquaintance, I venture to inquire; for two days there has been a trustworthy wind—the new man has already taken the throne; what need for concealment?"

units.zh: 張乃說：「來時聞李嗣源過河，未知近事。」
units.en: Zhang then admitted, "When I set out I heard Li Siyuan had crossed the Yellow River, but I do not know what has happened since."
units.literal: Zhang then said: "When I came I heard Li Siyuan had crossed the river; I do not know recent affairs."

units.zh: 岷曰：「魏王且請盤桓，以觀其勢，未可前邁。」
units.en: Chen said, "Prince Wei ought to hold where he is and watch how the situation develops. He must not press forward yet."
units.literal: Chen said: "Prince Wei should please linger and observe how matters stand; he must not advance yet."

units.zh: 張以莊宗命嚴，不敢遷延，督令進發，魏王至渭南遇害。）〉
units.en: Bound by Zhuangzong's strict order, Zhang would not delay and drove the march forward; Prince Wei reached Weinan and was killed.)〉
units.literal: Because Emperor Zhuangzong's command was strict, Zhang dared not delay and pressed for departure; Prince Wei reached Weinan and met disaster.)〉

units.zh: 繼潼、繼嵩、繼蟾、繼嶢並莊宗子，同光三年拜光祿大夫、檢校司徒，未封。
units.en: Jitong, Jisong, Jichan, and Jiyao were all sons of Zhuangzong. In Tongguang 3 they were made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and honorary Ministers of Education, but received no princely titles.
units.literal: Jitong, Jisong, Jichan, and Jiyao were all sons of Emperor Zhuangzong; in the third year of Tongguang they were appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and honorary Minister of Education, but were not enfeoffed.

units.zh: 莊宗敗，並不知所終。
units.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, none of their fates was ever learned.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, the end of all was unknown.

units.zh: 〈（《清異錄》：唐福慶公主下降孟知祥。
units.en: (Records of Pure Wonders records that Princess Fuqing of Tang was given in marriage to Meng Zhixiang.
units.literal: (Records of Pure Wonders: Princess Fuqing of Tang was married down to Meng Zhixiang.

units.zh: 長興四年，明宗晏駕，唐室亂。
units.en: In Changxing 4, when Emperor Mingzong died, the Tang court collapsed into chaos.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing, Emperor Mingzong died, and the Tang house fell into disorder.

units.zh: 莊宗諸兒削髮為芻，間道走蜀。
units.en: Zhuangzong's sons shaved their heads like common monks and stole away to Shu by back roads.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong's sons shaved their heads and became straw monks, fleeing by hidden paths to Shu.

units.zh: 時知祥新稱帝，為分主厚待猶子，賜予千計。）〉
units.en: Meng Zhixiang had just proclaimed himself emperor; treating them as kin of the fallen house, he received Zhuangzong's sons with great favor and showered them with gifts by the thousand.)〉
units.literal: At that time Zhixiang had newly declared himself emperor; as a kinsman of the divided ruler he treated the nephews generously, bestowing gifts by the thousands.)〉

units.zh: 從璟，明宗長子，性忠勇沈厚，摧堅陷陣，人罕偕焉。
units.en: Congjing, Mingzong's eldest son, was loyal, brave, and steady by nature; in smashing enemy lines few could stand beside him.
units.literal: Congjing, eldest son of Emperor Mingzong, was by nature loyal, brave, grave, and steady; in breaking hard lines and storming formations few could match him.

units.zh: 從莊宗於河上，累有戰功，莊宗器賞之，用為金槍指揮使。
units.en: He followed Zhuangzong on the Yellow River campaigns and won repeated victories; Zhuangzong prized him and appointed him commander of the Golden Spear Guard.
units.literal: Following Emperor Zhuangzong on the Yellow River front he repeatedly achieved battle merit; Zhuangzong valued and rewarded him and made him commander of the Golden Spear Guard.

units.zh: 明宗在魏府為軍士所逼，莊宗詔從璟曰：「爾父於國有大功，忠孝之心，朕自明信，今為亂兵所劫，爾宜自去宣朕旨，無令有疑。」
units.en: When Mingzong at Weifu was seized by mutinous troops, Zhuangzong sent Congjing this command: "Your father has rendered great service to the state, and I trust his loyalty without question. He is now held by rebellious soldiers. Go yourself and proclaim my will so that no suspicion remains."
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong at Weifu was pressed by soldiers, Emperor Zhuangzong issued an edict to Congjing: "Your father has great merit to the state; I myself trust his heart of loyalty and filial piety. Now that he is seized by mutinous troops, you should go yourself to proclaim my intent and let there be no doubt."

units.zh: 從璟行至中途，為元行欽所製，復與歸洛下。
units.en: Congjing had not gone far when Yuan Xingqin seized him and brought him back to Luoyang.
units.literal: Congjing had gone halfway when he was seized by Yuan Xingqin and brought back down to Luoyang.

units.zh: 莊宗改其名為繼璟，以為己子，命再往，從璟固執不行，願死於御前，以明丹赤。
units.en: Zhuangzong renamed him Jijing and treated him as a son, then ordered him to go again. Congjing refused outright, saying he would rather die before the throne than leave his loyalty in doubt.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong changed his name to Jijing, treating him as his own son, and ordered him to go again; Congjing firmly refused to go, wishing to die before the throne to make clear his loyal heart.

units.zh: 從莊宗赴汴州，明宗之親舊多策馬而去，左右或勸從璟令自脫，終無行意，尋為元行欽所殺。
units.en: When Zhuangzong marched toward Bianzhou, many of Mingzong's kinsmen and old friends rode away. His attendants urged Congjing to flee on his own, but he would not budge, and soon Yuan Xingqin killed him.
units.literal: Following Emperor Zhuangzong to Bianzhou, many of Mingzong's kin and old associates spurred their horses and left; those at Congjing's side sometimes urged him to escape on his own, but he never had the intent to go, and soon was killed by Yuan Xingqin.

units.zh: 天成初，贈太保。
units.en: At the opening of Tiancheng he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 秦王從榮，明宗第二子也。
units.en: Prince Qin Congrong was Mingzong's second son.
units.literal: Prince Qin Congrong was Emperor Mingzong's second son.

units.zh: 明宗踐阼，天成初，授鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne, in early Tiancheng Congrong was made Protector of Ye Capital and military commissioner of the Tianxiong army.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong ascended the throne, at the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed Protector of Ye Capital and military commissioner of Tianxiong Army.

units.zh: 三年，移北京留守，充河東節度使。
units.en: In the third year he was moved to Protector of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Northern Capital Protector and served as military commissioner of Hedong.

units.zh: 四年，入為河南尹。
units.en: In the fourth year he was appointed Intendant of Henan.
units.literal: In the fourth year he entered court as Intendant of Henan.

units.zh: 一日，明宗謂安重誨曰：「 近聞從榮左右有詐宣朕旨，令勿接儒生，儒生多懦，恐鈍誌相染。
units.en: One day Mingzong said to An Chonghui, "I have lately heard that men around Congrong are falsely speaking in my name, telling him not to receive Confucian scholars—scholars are too timid, they say, and might dull his ambition.
units.literal: One day Emperor Mingzong said to An Chonghui: "Recently I have heard that those around Congrong falsely proclaim my intent, ordering that Confucian scholars not be received, saying scholars are mostly timid and fear their dull wills will be infected.

units.zh: 朕方知之，頗駭其事。
units.en: I have only just learned of this, and it alarms me greatly.
units.literal: I have just learned of it and am greatly alarmed by the matter.

units.zh: 餘比以從榮方幼，出臨大藩，故先儒雅，賴其裨佐。
units.en: I sent scholars to him earlier because he was still young when he went out to govern a great circuit, and I relied on them to guide him.
units.literal: Previously, because Congrong was still young and had gone out to govern a great frontier, I first placed literati with him, relying on them to assist.

units.zh: 今聞此奸憸之言，豈朕之所望屯。」
units.en: To hear such treacherous talk now—this is not what I wanted at all."
units.literal: Now to hear such treacherous and sly words—how could this be what I hoped for?"

units.zh: 鞫其言者將戮之，重誨曰：「若遽行刑，又慮賓從難處，且望嚴誡。」
units.en: He was about to interrogate and execute the men responsible. Chonghui said, "If you execute them at once, his staff may become impossible to manage. I would ask only for a stern warning for now."
units.literal: He was about to interrogate and execute those who had spoken thus. Chonghui said: "If execution is carried out at once, I also fear his retainers will be hard to manage; I hope only for stern admonition for now."

units.zh: 遂止。
units.en: Mingzong relented.
units.literal: And so he stopped.

units.zh: 從榮為詩，與從事高輦等更相唱和，自謂章句獨步於一時，有詩千餘首，號曰《紫府集》。
units.en: Congrong wrote poetry and exchanged verses with his staff officer Gao Nian and others, claiming that in his generation no one matched his lines. He compiled more than a thousand poems under the title Collected Works of the Purple Palace.
units.literal: Congrong composed poetry, exchanging verses with his staff member Gao Nian and others, claiming his lines alone stood unmatched in his age; he had more than a thousand poems, titled Collected Works of the Purple Palace.

units.zh: 長興中，以本官充天下兵馬大元帥。
units.en: During the Changxing era he was appointed Grand Marshal of All Armies and Horses Under Heaven while retaining his existing rank.
units.literal: During Changxing he served in his existing office as Grand Marshal of All Armies and Horses Under Heaven.

units.zh: 從榮乃請以嚴衛、捧聖步騎兩指揮為秦府衙兵，每入朝，以數百騎從行，出則張弓挾矢，馳騁盈巷。
units.en: Congrong then asked that the Yanwei and Pingsheng infantry and cavalry commands serve as his Qin Palace guard. Whenever he attended court, several hundred horsemen escorted him; when he went abroad he rode with bow strung and arrows at hand, filling the streets with his galloping retinue.
units.literal: Congrong then requested that the two commands Yanwei and Pingsheng infantry and cavalry serve as Qin Palace guard troops; each time he entered court several hundred horsemen followed him, and when he went out he strung bows and carried arrows, galloping until the lanes were full.

units.zh: 既受元帥之命，即令其府屬僚佐及四方遊士，各試《檄淮南書》一道，陳己將廓清宇內之意。
units.en: After receiving the marshal's commission, he ordered his staff and visiting scholars from every quarter each to draft a Proclamation to Huainan proclaiming his intent to bring order to the empire.
units.literal: Once he had received the marshal's commission, he ordered his staff officers and wandering scholars from all quarters each to draft a Proclamation to Huainan, setting forth his intent to pacify the realm.

units.zh: 初，言事者請為親王置師傅，明宗顧問近臣，執政以從榮名勢既隆，不敢忤旨，即奏云：「王官宜委。」
units.en: Earlier, officials had urged that tutors be appointed for the prince. Mingzong consulted his close advisers, but the chief ministers, knowing Congrong's power was already formidable, dared not cross him and memorialized, "Let the prince choose his own staff."
units.literal: Earlier, memorialists had asked that tutors be appointed for the imperial prince. Emperor Mingzong consulted his close ministers; the chief ministers, because Congrong's fame and power were already lofty, dared not oppose his wishes and memorialized: "The prince's staff should be left to his discretion."

units.zh: 從榮乃奏刑部侍郎劉讚為王傅，又奏翰林學士崔棁為元帥府判官。
units.en: Congrong then nominated Vice Minister of Justice Liu Zan as his tutor and Hanlin Academician Cui Zhuo as chief administrator of the marshal's headquarters.
units.literal: Congrong then memorialized for Vice Minister of Justice Liu Zan as prince tutor and for Hanlin Academician Cui Zhuo as chief administrator of the marshal's headquarters.

units.zh: 明宗曰：「學士代予詔令，不可擬議。」
units.en: Mingzong said, "A Hanlin academician drafts my edicts; that nomination cannot stand."
units.literal: Emperor Mingzong said: "An academician drafts edicts in my place; he cannot be put forward for such a post."

units.zh: 衣榮不悅，退謂左右曰：「既付以元帥之任，而阻予請僚佐，又未諭製旨也。」
units.en: Congrong was displeased. Withdrawing, he told his attendants, "I am given the marshal's command, yet my choice of staff is blocked—and no explanation of the emperor's intent is offered."
units.literal: Congrong was displeased; withdrawing he said to those around him: "Having entrusted me with the marshal's charge, yet blocking my request for staff and not even explaining the imperial intent."

units.zh: 復奏刑部侍郎任讚，從之。
units.en: He then nominated Vice Minister of Justice Ren Zan, and the emperor approved.
units.literal: He memorialized again for Vice Minister of Justice Ren Zan, and the request was granted.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·趙上交傳》：秦王從榮開府兼判軍衛，以上交為虞部員外郎，充六軍諸衛推官。
units.en: (The Song History, biography of Zhao Shangjiao, records that when Prince Qin Congrong opened his headquarters and concurrently judged the army guards, Shangjiao was made Vice Director of the Bureau of Parks and investigating officer of the Six Armies and various guards.
units.literal: (Song History·Biography of Zhao Shangjiao: When Prince Qin Congrong opened his headquarters and concurrently judged the army guards, Shangjiao was made Vice Director of the Bureau of Parks and served as investigating officer of the Six Armies and various guards.

units.zh: 李澣、張沆、魚崇遠皆白衣在秦府，悉與上交友善。
units.en: Li Han, Zhang Hang, and Yu Chongyuan, all commoners at the Qin Palace, became his close friends.
units.literal: Li Han, Zhang Hang, and Yu Chongyuan were all commoners in the Qin Palace and all became close friends with Shangjiao.

units.zh: 累遷司封郎中，充判官。
units.en: He rose through promotion to Director of the Bureau of Seals and served as chief administrator.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Seals and served as chief administrator.

units.zh: 從榮素豪邁，不遵禮法，好昵群小，上交從容言曰：「王位尊嚴，當修令德以慰民望。
units.en: Congrong was by nature bold and lawless, fond of low company. Shangjiao said gently, "Your station is exalted; you should cultivate virtue to meet the people's hopes.
units.literal: Congrong by nature was bold and unrestrained, heedless of ritual and law, fond of intimacy with petty men. Shangjiao said calmly: "The prince's station is august; you should cultivate fine virtue to satisfy the people's hopes.

units.zh: 王忍為此，獨不見恭世子、戾太子之事乎？」
units.en: Can you persist in this and not see what became of the Heir of Gong and the Rebellious Heir?"
units.literal: Can the prince bear to act thus—have you alone not seen what befell the Heir of Gong and the Rebellious Heir?"

units.zh: 從榮怒，出之。
units.en: Congrong flew into a rage and dismissed him.
units.literal: Congrong was angry and expelled him.

units.zh: 曆涇、秦二鎮節度判官。
units.en: He later served as military administrator of the Jing and Qin circuits.
units.literal: He successively served as military administrator of the Jing and Qin circuits.

units.zh: 從榮及禍，僚屬皆坐斥。
units.en: When Congrong fell, his entire staff was punished and dismissed.
units.literal: When Congrong met disaster, his staff were all punished and expelled.

units.zh: 上交由是知名。）〉
units.en: Shangjiao thereby won renown.)〉
units.literal: Shangjiao thereby became well known.)〉

units.zh: 後舉兵犯宮室，敗死，廢為庶人。
units.en: Later he raised troops against the palace, was defeated and killed, and was posthumously degraded to commoner status.
units.literal: Later he raised troops and attacked the palace; defeated, he died, and was degraded to commoner status.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒·明宗紀》云：己丑，大漸，秦王從榮入問疾，帝俯首不能舉。
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror, annals of Mingzong, records that on jichou the emperor's illness grew grave. Prince Qin Congrong came to inquire after him, but the emperor could only bow his head and could not lift it.
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror·Annals of Mingzong states: On jichou the illness grew grave. Prince Qin Congrong entered to inquire after the emperor's health; the emperor bowed his head and could not raise it.

units.zh: 王淑妃曰：「從榮在此。」
units.en: Consort Wang Shufei said, "Congrong is here."
units.literal: Consort Wang Shufei said: "Congrong is here."

units.zh: 帝不應。
units.en: The emperor did not answer.
units.literal: The emperor did not respond.

units.zh: 從榮出，聞宮中皆哭。
units.en: Congrong left and heard weeping throughout the palace.
units.literal: Congrong went out and heard everyone in the palace weeping.

units.zh: 從榮意帝已殂，明旦，稱疾不入。
units.en: Congrong assumed the emperor was already dead; the next morning he pleaded illness and did not attend court.
units.literal: Congrong thought the emperor had already died; the next morning he claimed illness and did not enter.

units.zh: 是夕，帝實小愈，而從榮不知。
units.en: That night the emperor had in fact improved slightly, but Congrong did not know.
units.literal: That evening the emperor had in fact improved slightly, but Congrong did not know.

units.zh: 從榮自知不為時論所與，恐不得為嗣，與其黨謀，欲以兵入侍，先製權臣。
units.en: Knowing he lacked support and fearing he would not succeed to the throne, Congrong plotted with his faction to march in with troops, attend the emperor, and first overpower the powerful ministers.
units.literal: Congrong knew himself not favored by current opinion and feared he would not succeed; with his faction he plotted to enter with troops to attend the emperor and first subdue the powerful ministers.

units.zh: 壬辰，從榮自河南府常服將步騎千人陳於天津橋。
units.en: On renchen Congrong left Henan Prefecture in ordinary dress at the head of a thousand foot and horse and formed ranks at Tianjin Bridge.
units.literal: On renchen Congrong, in ordinary dress from Henan Prefecture, led a thousand infantry and cavalry and drew them up at Tianjin Bridge.

units.zh: 孟漢瓊被甲乘馬，召馬軍都指揮使朱洪實，使將五百騎討從榮，從榮方據胡床，坐橋上，遣左右召康義誠。
units.en: Meng Hanqiong donned armor, mounted his horse, and summoned Horse Army Commander Zhu Hongshi to lead five hundred cavalry against Congrong. Congrong was lounging on a camp chair on the bridge and sent attendants to summon Kang Yicheng.
units.literal: Meng Hanqiong donned armor and mounted a horse, summoned Horse Army Commander Zhu Hongshi, and ordered him to lead five hundred cavalry against Congrong. Congrong was just then reclining on a folding chair, seated on the bridge, and sent his attendants to summon Kang Yicheng.

units.zh: 端門已閉，叩左掖門，從門隙窺之，見朱洪實引騎兵北來，走白從榮，從榮大驚，命取鐵掩心擐之，坐調弓矢。
units.en: The main gate was shut; he knocked at the Left Flank Gate and peered through the crack, saw Zhu Hongshi leading cavalry northward, and ran to warn Congrong. Congrong was terrified, ordered iron breastplates brought and put on, and sat stringing his bow.
units.literal: The Gate of Correct Deportment was already closed; he knocked at the Left Flank Gate and peered through the crack, saw Zhu Hongshi leading cavalry northward, ran to report to Congrong. Congrong was greatly alarmed, ordered iron breastplates brought and donned, and sat adjusting bow and arrows.

units.zh: 俄而騎兵大至，從榮走歸府，僚佐皆竄匿，牙兵掠嘉善坊潰去。
units.en: Soon the cavalry arrived in force. Congrong fled to his residence; his staff scattered and hid, and his guard soldiers looted Jia Shan Ward and melted away.
units.literal: Before long the cavalry arrived in force; Congrong fled back to his residence, his staff all hid and scattered, and the guard soldiers plundered Jia Shan Ward and broke in rout.

units.zh: 從榮與妃劉氏匿床下，皇城使安從益就斬之，以其首獻。
units.en: Congrong and his consort Lady Liu hid under a bed. Imperial City Commissioner An Congyi went in and beheaded him, presenting his head.
units.literal: Congrong and his consort Lady Liu hid under the bed; Imperial City Commissioner An Congyi went and beheaded him, presenting his head.

units.zh: 丙申，追廢從榮為庶人。
units.en: On bingshen he was posthumously degraded to commoner status.
units.literal: On bingshen Congrong was posthumously degraded to commoner status.

units.zh: 《五代會要》云：清泰元年，葬以公禮。
units.en: The Five Dynasties Institutional Essentials records that in Qingtai 1 he was buried with ducal rites.
units.literal: Five Dynasties Institutional Essentials states: In the first year of Qingtai he was buried with the rites due a duke.

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The court approved.
units.literal: The request was granted.

units.zh: 《五代史補》：秦王從榮，明宗之愛子。
units.en: The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties calls Prince Qin Congrong Mingzong's beloved son.
units.literal: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Prince Qin Congrong was Emperor Mingzong's beloved son.

units.zh: 好為詩，判河南府，辟高輦為推官。
units.en: He loved poetry; as judge of Henan Prefecture he recruited Gao Nian as investigating officer.
units.literal: He loved composing poetry; as judge of Henan Prefecture he recruited Gao Nian as investigating officer.

units.zh: 輦尤能為詩，賓主相遇甚歡。
units.en: Gao Nian was himself a fine poet, and prince and officer took great pleasure in each other's company.
units.literal: Nian was especially skilled at poetry; host and guest met in great delight.

units.zh: 自是出入門下者，當時名士有若張杭、高文蔚、何仲舉之徒，莫不分廷抗禮。
units.en: Thereafter the famous men who passed through his doors—Zhang Hang, Gao Wenwei, He Zhongju, and others—were all received as equals in his hall.
units.literal: From then on those who entered and left his gate—famous men of the time such as Zhang Hang, Gao Wenwei, He Zhongju, and the like—all shared the hall as equals.

units.zh: 更唱迭和。
units.en: They exchanged verses back and forth.
units.literal: They exchanged verses in turn.

units.zh: 時干戈之後，武夫用事，睹從榮所為，皆不悅。
units.en: In those days, after years of war, men of the sword held power, and they disliked everything they saw Congrong doing.
units.literal: At that time, after the wars, military men held power; seeing what Congrong did, they were all displeased.

units.zh: 於是康知訓等竊議曰：「秦王好文，交遊者多詞客，此子若一旦南面，則我等轉死溝壑，不如早圖之。」
units.en: Kang Zhixun and others whispered among themselves, "Prince Qin loves literature and keeps company with poets. If he ever takes the throne, we shall die in the ditches. Better to move against him now."
units.literal: Thereupon Kang Zhixun and others whispered: "Prince Qin loves letters; most of his companions are literary men. If this man one day faces south, we shall die in ditches and gullies—better to plot against him early."

units.zh: 高輦知其謀，因勸秦王托疾：「此輩須來問候，請大王伏壯士，出其不意皆斬之，庶幾免禍矣。」
units.en: Gao Nian learned of the plot and urged the prince to feign illness: "They will come to inquire after you. Hide strong men and cut them down by surprise—that may be your only escape."
units.literal: Gao Nian learned of their plot and therefore urged Prince Qin to feign illness: "These men will certainly come to inquire after you; I beg the prince to hide strong men and, taking them unawares, behead them all—then perhaps disaster may be avoided."

units.zh: 從榮曰：「至尊在上，一旦如此，得無危乎？」
units.en: Congrong said, "The emperor is still above us. To do such a thing—would it not be perilous?"
units.literal: Congrong said: "The sovereign is above us; to act thus all at once—would it not be dangerous?"

units.zh: 輦曰：「子弄父兵，罪當笞爾；
units.en: Gao Nian replied, "A son who misuses his father's soldiers deserves no more than a beating;
units.literal: Nian said: "A son who toys with his father's soldiers deserves only the lash;

units.zh: 不然，則悔無及矣。」
units.en: otherwise you will regret it when it is too late."
units.literal: otherwise regret will come too late."

units.zh: 從榮猶豫不決，未幾及禍，高輦棄市。
units.en: Congrong wavered and could not decide. Before long disaster struck, and Gao Nian was executed in the marketplace.
units.literal: Congrong hesitated and could not decide; before long he met disaster, and Gao Nian was executed in the marketplace.

units.zh: 初，從榮之敗也，高輦竄於民家，且落發為僧。
units.en: When Congrong fell, Gao Nian hid in a commoner's house and shaved his head to pass as a monk.
units.literal: Earlier, when Congrong was defeated, Gao Nian hid in a commoner's house and even shaved his head to become a monk.

units.zh: 既擒獲，知訓以其毀形難認，復使巾幘著緋，驗其真偽，然後用刑。
units.en: Once captured, Zhixun, finding his altered appearance hard to recognize, had him dressed again in cap and scarlet robe to confirm his identity before executing him.
units.literal: Once he was captured, Zhixun, because his altered appearance made him hard to recognize, had him again put on cap and scarlet robe to verify his identity, and only then applied punishment.

units.zh: 輦神色自若，屬聲曰：「朱衣才脫，白刃難逃。」
units.en: Gao Nian's face was calm. He cried aloud, "Scarlet robes just cast off—white blades you cannot escape."
units.literal: Nian's expression was calm; raising his voice he said: "Scarlet robes just removed, white blades cannot be escaped."

units.zh: 觀者笑之。）〉
units.en: The crowd laughed.)〉
units.literal: The onlookers laughed at him.)〉

units.zh: 從璨，明宗諸子。
units.en: Congcan was one of Mingzong's sons.
units.literal: Congcan was among Emperor Mingzong's sons.

units.zh: 性剛直，好客疏財，意豁如也。
units.en: He was upright and blunt by nature, hospitable and generous, open-hearted and free.
units.literal: By nature he was upright and blunt, hospitable to guests and free with wealth, open and generous in spirit.

units.zh: 天成中，為右衛大將軍，時安重誨方秉事權，從璨亦不之屈，重誨嘗以此忌之。
units.en: During Tiancheng he was Grand General of the Right Guard. An Chonghui then held power, and Congcan would not bow to him; Chonghui resented him for it.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he was Grand General of the Right Guard; at that time An Chonghui held governmental power, and Congcan would not yield to him—Chonghui often resented him for this.

units.zh: 明宗幸汴，留從璨為大內皇城使。
units.en: When Mingzong visited Bian, he left Congcan as commissioner of the inner imperial city.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong visited Bian, he left Congcan as commissioner of the inner imperial city.

units.zh: 一日，召賓友於會節園，酒酣之後，戲登於禦榻。
units.en: One day he summoned friends to Huijie Garden, and in his cups playfully climbed onto the imperial couch.
units.literal: One day he summoned guests and friends to Huijie Garden; after the wine had gone deep, in jest he climbed onto the imperial couch.

units.zh: 安重誨奏請誅之。
units.en: An Chonghui memorialized asking that he be executed.
units.literal: An Chonghui memorialized requesting his execution.

units.zh: 詔曰：「皇城使從璨，朕巡幸汴州，使警大內。
units.en: An edict declared, "Imperial City Commissioner Congcan: when We toured Bianzhou We charged him to guard the inner palace.
units.literal: An edict said: "Imperial City Commissioner Congcan—when We toured Bianzhou We ordered him to guard the inner palace.

units.zh: 乃全乖委任，但恣遨遊，於予行從之園，頻恣歌歡之會，仍施峻法，顯辱平人，致彼喧嘩，達於聞聽。
units.en: Yet he wholly betrayed that trust, roaming in pleasure alone. In the garden of Our traveling suite he held repeated revels of song and wine, applied harsh punishments, openly humiliated common people, and stirred uproar that reached Our ears.
units.literal: Yet he wholly betrayed the commission, indulging only in roaming pleasure; in the garden of Our traveling suite he repeatedly held riotous song and revel, still applied harsh law, and openly shamed common people, causing uproar that reached Our ears.

units.zh: 方當立法，固不黨親，宜貶授房州司戶參軍，仍令盡命。」
units.en: Law must be upheld and kinship cannot shield him. He is demoted to Army Aide of Fangzhou, and his life is forfeit."
units.literal: Now that law is to be upheld, kinship shall not shield him; he should be demoted and appointed Army Aide of Fangzhou, and his life is forfeit."

units.zh: 長興中，重誨之得罪也。
units.en: During Changxing, when Chonghui fell from power,
units.literal: During Changxing, when Chonghui fell from grace,

units.zh: 命復舊官，仍贈太保。
units.en: Congcan's former office was restored and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: an order restored his former office and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 許王從益，明宗之幼子也。
units.en: Prince Xu Congyi was Mingzong's youngest son.
units.literal: Prince Xu Congyi was Emperor Mingzong's youngest son.

units.zh: 宮嬪所生。
units.en: He was born to a palace concubine.
units.literal: He was born of a palace concubine.

units.zh: 明宗命王淑妃母之，嘗謂左右曰：「惟此兒生於皇宮，故尤所鍾愛。」
units.en: Mingzong appointed Consort Wang Shufei as his foster mother and once told his attendants, "Only this child was born in the palace itself, and so I cherish him above all."
units.literal: Emperor Mingzong ordered Consort Wang Shufei to be his foster mother and once said to those around him: "Only this child was born within the imperial palace, and so I especially cherish him."

units.zh: 長興末，封許王。
units.en: At the end of the Changxing era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.
units.literal: At the end of Changxing he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.

units.zh: 晉高祖即位，以皇后即其姊也，乃養從益於宮中。
units.en: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, the empress being his elder sister, Congyi was raised in the palace.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, because the empress was his elder sister, Congyi was raised within the palace.

units.zh: 晉天福中，以從益為二王後，改封郇國公，食邑三千戶。
units.en: During Jin Tianfu he was made heir to the second princely rank, retitled Duke of Xun, with a fief of three thousand households.
units.literal: During Tianfu of Jin, Congyi was made heir to the second prince rank, his title was changed to Duke of Xun, and his fief was three thousand households.

units.zh: 其後與母歸洛陽。
units.en: He later returned to Luoyang with his mother.
units.literal: Afterward he returned to Luoyang with his mother.

units.zh: 守陵開運末，契丹主至汴，以從益遙領曹州節度使，復封許王，與王妃尋歸西京。
units.en: While guarding the imperial tombs in late Kaiyun, the Khitan ruler reached Bian. Congyi was given titular command of Caozhou, again enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, and soon returned to the Western Capital with his consort.
units.literal: While guarding the tombs at the end of Kaiyun, the Khitan ruler came to Bian; Congyi was made titular military commissioner of Caozhou at a distance, again enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, and soon returned to the Western Capital with his princess consort.

units.zh: 會契丹主死，其汴州節度使蕭翰謀歸北地，慮中原無主，軍民大亂，則己亦不得按轡徐歸矣；
units.en: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north. He feared that with no ruler in the Central Plains and army and people in chaos, he himself could not withdraw at leisure;
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north and feared that with no ruler in central China and army and people in great disorder, he himself would be unable to rein in his horse and withdraw at leisure;

units.zh: 乃詐稱契丹主命，遣人迎從益於洛陽，令知南朝軍國事。
units.en: so he falsely claimed the Khitan ruler's command, sent men to summon Congyi from Luoyang, and installed him to govern the southern court's military and civil affairs.
units.literal: therefore he falsely claimed the Khitan ruler's command, sent men to welcome Congyi from Luoyang, and ordered him to manage the military and civil affairs of the southern court.

units.zh: 從益與王妃逃於徽陵以避之，使者至，不得已而赴焉。
units.en: Congyi and his consort fled to Huiling to escape the summons; when the envoys arrived, he had no choice but to go.
units.literal: Congyi and his princess consort fled to Huiling to avoid this; when the envoys arrived, unable to refuse, he went to them.

units.zh: 從益於崇元殿見群官。
units.en: Congyi received the assembled officials in Chongyuan Hall.
units.literal: Congyi received the assembled officials in Chongyuan Hall.

units.zh: 蕭翰率蕃首列拜於殿上，群官趨於殿下，乃偽署王鬆為左丞相，趙上交為右丞相。
units.en: Xiao Han led the Khitan chiefs in ranks bowing in the hall while the officials hurried to below the steps. He falsely appointed Wang Song Left Chancellor and Zhao Shangjiao Right Chancellor.
units.literal: Xiao Han led the Khitan chiefs in ranks bowing in the hall; the officials hurried to below the steps, and he falsely appointed Wang Song as Left Chancellor and Zhao Shangjiao as Right Chancellor.

units.zh: 李式、翟光鄴為樞密使，王景崇為宣徽使，餘官各有署置。
units.en: Li Shi and Zhai Guangye were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wang Jingchong palace commissioner, and the remaining posts were each filled.
units.literal: Li Shi and Zhai Guangye were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wang Jingchong was made palace commissioner, and the remaining offices were each filled.

units.zh: 又以北來燕將劉祚為權侍衛使，充在京巡檢。
units.en: The Yan general Liu Zuo, newly arrived from the north, was made acting commissioner of the Palace Guard and charged with capital patrol.
units.literal: Furthermore the Yan general Liu Zuo, who had come from the north, was made acting commissioner of the Palace Guard and charged with patrol in the capital.

units.zh: 翰北歸，從益餞於北郊。
units.en: When Xiao Han marched north, Congyi gave him a farewell feast at the Northern Suburb.
units.literal: When Han returned north, Congyi gave a farewell feast at the Northern Suburb.

units.zh: 及漢高祖將離太原，從益召高行周、武行德欲拒漢高祖，行周等不從，且奏其事。
units.en: When Gaozu of Han was about to march from Taiyuan, Congyi summoned Gao Xingzhou and Wu Xingde to resist him. They refused and memorialized the court.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Han was about to leave Taiyuan, Congyi summoned Gao Xingzhou and Wu Xingde, wishing to resist Gaozu of Han; Xingzhou and the others would not obey and moreover memorialized the matter.

units.zh: 漢高祖怒，車駕將至闕，從益與王妃俱賜死於私第，時年十七；
units.en: Gaozu of Han was enraged. As the imperial carriage neared the capital, Congyi and his consort were both ordered to die in their private residence. He was seventeen;
units.literal: Gaozu of Han was angry; as the imperial carriage was about to reach the palace, Congyi and his princess consort were both granted death in their private residence; he was seventeen years old;

units.zh: 時人哀之。
units.en: and the people pitied him.
units.literal: people of the time pitied him.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：漢高祖自太原起軍建號，至洛陽，會郭從義先入京師，受密旨殺王淑妃與許王從益。
units.en: (Lost Writings of the History of the Five Dynasties records that Gaozu of Han raised his army at Taiyuan and established his reign. Reaching Luoyang, he found Guo Congyi already in the capital with a secret order to kill Consort Wang Shufei and Prince Xu Congyi.
units.literal: (Lost Writings of the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu of Han raised an army at Taiyuan and established his reign; reaching Luoyang, he met Guo Congyi, who had entered the capital first and received a secret order to kill Consort Wang Shufei and Prince Xu Congyi.

units.zh: 淑妃臨刑號泣曰：「吾家子母何罪，吾既為契丹所立，非敢與人爭國，何不且留吾兒，每年寒食，使持一盂飯灑明宗陵寢。」
units.en: Facing execution the consort wept aloud, "What crime have mother and son committed? The Khitan installed me; I never sought to contend for the realm. Why not spare my son, so that each Cold Food he may bring one bowl of rice to Mingzong's tomb?"
units.literal: Facing execution the consort wept aloud: "What crime have my household's mother and son committed? I was installed by the Khitan and did not dare contend for the realm with others—why not at least spare my son, so that each year at Cold Food he may bring one bowl of rice to pour at Emperor Mingzong's tomb?"

units.zh: 聞者無不泣下。）〉
units.en: All who heard wept.)〉
units.literal: All who heard wept.)〉

units.zh: 重吉，末帝長子，為控鶴都指揮使。
units.en: Chongji, the Last Emperor's eldest son, was director of the Crane-Control Directorate.
units.literal: Chongji, the Last Emperor's eldest son, served as director of the Crane-Control Directorate.

units.zh: 閔帝嗣位，出為亳州團練使。
units.en: When Emperor Min succeeded, he was posted out as training commissioner of Bozhou.
units.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, he was posted out as training commissioner of Bozhou.

units.zh: 末帝兵起，為閔帝所害。
units.en: When the Last Emperor raised his army, Emperor Min had him killed.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor raised his army, he was killed by Emperor Min.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：詔遣殿直楚匡祚執亳州李重吉，幽於宋州。
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that an edict dispatched Palace Guard Chu Kuangzuo to arrest Li Chongji of Bozhou and imprison him at Songzhou.
units.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: An edict dispatched Palace Guard Chu Kuangzuo to arrest Li Chongji of Bozhou and imprison him at Songzhou.

units.zh: 又云：遣楚匡祚殺李重吉於宋州。
units.en: It also records that Chu Kuangzuo was sent to kill Li Chongji at Songzhou.
units.literal: It also states: Chu Kuangzuo was sent to kill Li Chongji at Songzhou.

units.zh: 匡祚榜捶重吉，責其家財。）〉
units.en: Kuangzuo beat Chongji with cudgels and extorted his family's wealth.)〉
units.literal: Kuangzuo beat Chongji with cudgels and extorted his family's wealth.)〉

units.zh: 清泰元年，詔贈太尉，仍令宋州選隙地置廟。
units.en: In Qingtai 1 an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal and ordered Songzhou to select vacant land for a temple.
units.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal and ordered Songzhou to select vacant land on which to establish a temple.

units.zh: 〈（《明宗紀》：閔帝有子重哲，授銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書。
units.en: (The Annals of Emperor Mingzong note that Emperor Min had a son Chongzhe, appointed Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Proper Counsel and honorary Minister of Works.
units.literal: (Annals of Emperor Mingzong: Emperor Min had a son Chongzhe, appointed Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Proper Counsel and honorary Minister of Works.

units.zh: 《歐陽史·家人傳》闕而不載，今附識於此。）〉
units.en: The Ouyang History's "Family Biographies" omits this entry; it is appended here for reference.)〉
units.literal: The Ouyang History's "Family Biographies" omits this; it is appended here for reference.)〉

units.zh: 雍王理美，末帝第二子，清泰三年封。
units.en: Prince Yong Limei, the Last Emperor's second son, was enfeoffed in Qingtai 3.
units.literal: Prince Yong Limei, the Last Emperor's second son, was enfeoffed in the third year of Qingtai.

units.zh: 晉兵入，與末帝俱自焚死。
units.en: When the Jin army entered Luoyang, he and the Last Emperor burned themselves to death.
units.literal: When the Jin army entered, he and the Last Emperor both burned themselves to death.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：洛陽自聞兵敗，眾心大震，居人四出，逃竄山谷。
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that from the moment Luoyang heard of the army's defeat, panic seized the city and residents fled into the hills on every side.
units.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: From the time Luoyang heard of the army's defeat, popular hearts were greatly shaken; residents went out on all sides, fleeing into valleys and hills.

units.zh: 門者請禁之，雍王重美曰：「國家多難，未能為百姓主，又禁其求生，徒增惡名耳。
units.en: The gatekeepers asked to stop them. Prince Yong Chongmei said, "The state is in grave trouble and cannot yet protect its people. To forbid them to save themselves would only deepen our ill repute.
units.literal: The gatekeepers asked to forbid it. Prince Yong Chongmei said: "The state has many hardships and cannot yet be master to the people; to forbid their seeking life would only add to ill repute.

units.zh: 不若聽其自便，事寧自還。」
units.en: Better to let them go where they will; when peace returns they will come back."
units.literal: Better to let them go as they please; when matters are settled they will return of themselves."

units.zh: 乃出令任從所適，眾心差安。
units.en: He issued an order allowing people to go where they wished, and the city grew somewhat calmer.
units.literal: He then issued an order allowing people to go where they wished, and hearts were somewhat calmed.

units.zh: 又云：皇后積薪欲燒宮室，重美諫曰：「新天子至，必不露居，他日重勞民力，死而遺怨，將安用之。」
units.en: The text also records that the empress piled firewood to burn the palace. Chongmei remonstrated, "The new emperor will not live in the open air. To burn the palace would burden the people again after your death and leave only resentment. What good would that do?"
units.literal: It also states: The empress piled firewood intending to burn the palace buildings. Chongmei remonstrated: "When the new Son of Heaven arrives he will surely not live exposed to the elements; another day you would burden the people's strength again—dead yet leaving resentment behind; what use is there in it?"

units.zh: 乃止。）〉
units.en: She desisted.)〉
units.literal: And so she stopped.)〉

units.zh: 史臣曰：繼岌以童騃之歲，當統帥之任，雖功成於劍外，尋求死於渭濱，蓋運盡天亡，非孺子之咎也。
units.en: The historiographer remarks: Jiji bore a commander's charge while still a child. Though he won glory beyond the Sword Gate, he soon met death on the Wei River—fortune had run its course and heaven had spoken; the fault was not that of a boy.
units.literal: The historiographer remarks: Jiji, in the tender years of childhood, bore the commander's charge; though he achieved merit beyond Jianmen, he soon sought death on the Wei River's bank—this was fortune exhausted and heaven's decree, not the fault of a young boy.

units.zh: 從審感厚遇之恩，無苟免之意，死於君側，得不謂之忠乎！
units.en: Congshen repaid generous treatment with loyalty, refusing any easy escape, and died at his lord's side. Can this be called anything but faithful devotion?
units.literal: Congshen felt deep gratitude for generous treatment and had no thought of easy escape; he died at his lord's side—can this not be called loyalty!

units.zh: 從榮以狂躁之謀，賈覆亡之禍，謂為大逆，則近厚誣。
units.en: Congrong, through rash and reckless plotting, brought ruin on himself. To call it high treason comes close to slander.
units.literal: Congrong, through rash and reckless plotting, bought the calamity of ruin; to call it great treason comes close to gross slander.

units.zh: 從璨為權臣所忌，從益為強敵所脅，俱不得其死，亦良可傷哉！
units.en: Congcan was destroyed by a powerful minister, Congyi was coerced by a strong enemy—neither died a natural death. How lamentable!
units.literal: Congcan was resented by a powerful minister, Congyi was coerced by a strong enemy—neither met a natural death; this too is deeply lamentable!

units.zh: 重美聽洛民之奔亡，止母後之燔爇，身雖燼於戲焰，言則耀乎青編。
units.en: Chongmei allowed the people of Luoyang to flee and stopped the empress from burning the palace. Though his body perished in the flames, his words shine in the annals.
units.literal: Chongmei allowed the people of Luoyang to flee, stopped the empress from burning the palace—though his body was consumed in playful flame, his words shine in the blue-bound annals.

units.zh: 童年若斯，可謂賢矣！
units.en: For one so young, he may truly be called worthy!
units.literal: At such a young age, he may be called worthy!

units.zh: 龍德末，閑居私第將期矣，晉主入汴，振謁見首罪，郭崇韜指振謂人曰：「人言李振乃一代奇才，吾今見之，乃常人耳！」
units.en: At the end of Longde he had lived in retirement nearly a year; when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen came to beg mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at him and said: "They call Li Zhen a wonder of the age—I see an ordinary man!"
units.literal: End of Longde, living in retirement at his private residence nearly a year, when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen paid court asking mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at Zhen and said to people: "People say Li Zhen is a generation's strange talent—I see him now and he is just an ordinary man!"

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 裨將趙在禮聞軍亂，衣不及帶，將逾垣而遁，亂兵追及，白刃環之曰：「公能為帥否？
units.en: Lieutenant Zhao Zaili, hearing the army was in chaos, had no time to belt his robe and was about to climb over the wall to flee when the mutineers caught him; blades ringed him and they said, "Can you be commander?
units.literal: Lieutenant Zhao Zaili, hearing the army in chaos, had not time to belt his robe and was about to climb the wall to flee when the mutineers overtook him; blades ringed him and they said, "Can you be commander?

units.zh: 在禮懼，即曰：「吾能為之。」
units.en: Terrified, Zhao Zaili immediately said, "I can do it."
units.literal: Terrified, Zhao Zaili immediately said, "I can do it."

units.zh: 詰旦，擁在禮趨臨清，剽永濟、館陶。
units.en: At dawn they marched Zhao Zaili toward Linqing and raided Yongji and Guantao.
units.literal: At dawn they drove Zaili toward Linqing and plundered Yongji and Guantao.

units.zh: 晡晚，趙在禮引諸軍據宮城，署皇甫暉等為都虞候、斬斫使，諸軍大掠。
units.en: By evening Zhao Zaili held the palace, made Huangfu Hui adjutant, and the army looted Ye.
units.literal: In late afternoon Zhao Zaili led the armies to seize the palace city, appointing Huangfu Hui and others overall adjutants and execution officers; the armies plundered greatly.

units.zh: 興唐尹王正言謁在禮，望塵再拜。
units.en: Wang Zhengyan bowed twice in the dust to Zhao Zaili.
units.literal: Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan called on Zaili and twice bowed in the dust.

units.zh: 是日，眾推在禮為兵馬留後，草奏以聞。
units.en: That day the mutineers made Zhao Zaili acting commissioner and memorialized court.
units.literal: That day the crowd pushed Zaili as acting military commissioner and drafted a memorial to report it.

units.zh: 辛丑，元行欽至鄴都，進攻南門，以詔書招諭城中，趙在禮獻羊酒勞軍，登城遙拜行欽曰：「將士經年離隔父母，不取敕旨歸寧，上貽聖憂，追悔何及！
units.en: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and used an edict to summon the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and bowed from the wall to Xingqin, saying, "The soldiers have been separated from their parents for years; by returning home without edict, they have burdened the sage with worry. What regret can suffice!
units.literal: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and with an edict summoned the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and from the wall bowed distantly to Xingqin, saying, "The troops were separated from parents for years and, not taking the edict to return home, burdened the sage—what regret can suffice!

units.zh: 眾遂呼噪，中夜燔劫貝郡。
units.en: The mutineers shouted and looted Beizhou at midnight.
units.literal: The crowd then shouted and at midnight burned and plundered Beizhou.

units.zh: 否則頭隨刃落！」
units.en: If not, your head will fall with the blade!"
units.literal: If not, your head follows the blade!"

units.zh: 儻公善為敷奏，俾從渙汗，某等亦不敢不改過自新。」
units.en: If you, sir, will memorialize well and let us follow the edict of grace, we too dare not fail to reform ourselves."
units.literal: If you, sir, will memorialize well and let us follow the edict of grace, we too dare not fail to reform."

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 癸亥，鎮州武行德、鳳翔趙暉並加檢校太師。
units.en: On guihai, Wu Xingde of Zhen Prefecture and Zhao Hui of Fengxiang were both given the additional title of Acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: On guihai, Zhen Prefecture Wu Xingde and Fengxiang Zhao Hui were both given the additional title of Acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 壬子，蜀主王衍致書於帝，稱有詐為天使，馳報收復汴州者，詔捕之，不獲。
units.en: On renzi Wang Yan of Shu wrote that a fake envoy had reported Bian recovered; Cunxu ordered arrest but found no one.
units.literal: On renzi Shu ruler Wang Yan wrote the Emperor that someone had falsely posed as an envoy and rushed word that Bian had been recovered; an edict ordered his arrest, but he was not caught.

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 乃以皇子繼岌為亞獻，皇弟存紀為終獻。
units.en: Jiji was made second libationer and Cunji final libationer.
units.literal: Prince Jiji was then made second libationer and the Emperor's brother Cunji final libationer.

units.zh: 以北京皇城留守、檢校太保、左威衛上將軍李存紀為邢州節度使，加檢校太傅；
units.en: Li Cunji, northern-capital imperial-city commandant, honorary Grand Guardian, and Left Awe Guard senior general, became military governor of Xing Prefecture and was additionally made honorary Grand Mentor;
units.literal: northern capital inner-city commandant, Grand Guardian, and General of the Left Awe Guards Li Cunji was made Xingzhou military commissioner and Grand Mentor;

units.zh: 是時，魏州妖人楊千郎用事，自言有墨子術，能役使鬼神，化丹砂、水銀。
units.en: The Wei sorcerer Yang Qianlang claimed Mohist arts to command spirits and transmute mercury.
units.literal: At that time the Wei sorcerer Yang Qianlang was in favor, claiming Mohist arts to command ghosts and spirits and turn cinnabar and mercury.

units.zh: 莊宗頗神之，拜千郎檢校尚書郎，賜紫，其妻出入宮禁，承恩寵，而士或因之以求官爵，存乂及存渥等往往朋淫於其家。
units.en: Zhuangzong made him acting director with purple robes; his wife entered the palace; Cunyi and Cunwo often caroused there.
units.literal: Zhuangzong treated him as miraculous, made him acting director of the Secretariat with purple robes; his wife entered the forbidden palace and received favor, and gentlemen often used him to seek office; Cunyi and Cunwo often debauched at his house.

units.zh: 及崇韜被族，莊宗遣宦官陰察外議以為如何，而宦官因欲盡誅崇韜親黨以絕後患，乃誣言：「存乂過千郎，酒酣，攘臂號泣，為婦翁稱冤，言甚怨望。」
units.en: When Chongtao’s clan was killed, eunuchs probed opinion and lied: "Cunyi, drunk at Qianlang’s house, had wailed for his father-in-law in rage."
units.literal: When Chongtao’s clan was exterminated Zhuangzong sent eunuchs to probe public opinion; the eunuchs wished to wipe out Chongtao’s kin to cut off future trouble and slandered: “Cunyi visited Qianlang; drunk, he waved his arms and wailed, crying injustice for his father-in-law, words full of resentment.”

units.zh: 莊宗大怒，以兵圍其第而誅之，並誅千郎。
units.en: Zhuangzong surrounded his house and killed him and Qianlang.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was furious, surrounded his residence with troops and executed him, and also executed Qianlang.

units.zh: 太祖子八人：莊宗長子也，次曰存美、存霸、存禮、存渥、存乂、存確、存紀。
units.en: Taizu had eight sons: Zhuangzong first, then Cunmei, Cunba, Cunli, Cunwo, Cunyi, Cunque, and Cunji.
units.literal: Taizu had eight sons: Zhuangzong was the eldest; next Cunmei, Cunba, Cunli, Cunwo, Cunyi, Cunque, and Cunji.

units.zh: 癸未，封唐許王李從益為郇國公，奉唐之祀，服色旌旗一依舊制。
units.en: On the guiwei day, Li Congyi, Prince of Xu of Tang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xun to maintain the sacrifices of Tang, with ceremonial dress, colors, and banners following the old Tang regulations.
units.literal: On the guiwei day, Li Congyi, Prince of Xu of Tang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xun to maintain the sacrifices of Tang; ceremonial dress, colors, and banners all followed the old regulations.

units.zh: 宜以郇國三千戶封唐許王李從益為郇國公」云。）〉
units.en: The three thousand households of Xun should enfeoff Li Congyi, Prince of Xu of Tang, as Duke of Xun," it states.)〉
units.literal: The three thousand households of the State of Xun should enfeoff Li Congyi, Prince of Xu of Tang, as Duke of Xun," it states.)〉

units.zh: 削木剪紙，皆無故事，班、墨之思，何以相過。」
units.en: Carving wood and cutting paper has no precedent—how could Ban and Mo's inventiveness be surpassed?"
units.literal: Carving wood and cutting paper—there is no precedent for that; how could the thought of Ban and Mo be surpassed?"

units.zh: 幸左龍武軍，以皇子繼岌代張全義判六軍諸衛事故也。
units.en: Cunxu visited the Left Dragon Martial Army as Prince Jiji took over Zhang Quanyi's charge of the Six Armies and Guards.
units.literal: The Emperor visited the Left Dragon Martial Army because the prince Jiji was replacing Zhang Quanyi in overseeing the Six Armies and Imperial Guards.

units.zh: 丁巳，永興都部署郭從義奏：「新除華州留後趙思綰，自今月三日授華州留後，準詔赴任，三移行期，仍要鎧甲以給牙兵，及與之，竟不遵路。
units.en: On dingsi, the Yongxing commander-in-chief Guo Congyi memorialized: "The newly appointed acting military governor of Hua, Zhao Sizhan, was appointed on the third of this month and should by edict proceed to his post. Three times the departure date was moved, yet he still demanded armor to supply his personal guard. When it was given him, in the end he did not take the road.
units.literal: On dingsi, the Yongxing commander-in-chief Guo Congyi memorialized: "The newly appointed acting military governor of Hua, Zhao Sizhan, from the third of this month when he was appointed acting governor of Hua, should by edict proceed to his post; three times the departure date was moved, yet he still demanded armor to supply his personal guard; when it was given him, in the end he did not take the road.

units.zh: 守溫有愛姬陷在賊城，為思綰所錄，及收城，從義盡得思綰之婢仆，守溫求其愛姬，從義雖與之，意有所慊，遂發前罪，密啟於郭威，請除之，與王益等並誅焉。
units.en: Shouwen had a beloved concubine trapped in the rebel city who had been taken by Sizhan. When the city was recovered, Congyi obtained all of Sizhan's maids and servants. Shouwen asked for his beloved concubine. Though Congyi gave her to him, he was not satisfied and exposed Shouwen's former crime, secretly reporting to Guo Wei and requesting his removal. Shouwen and Wang Yi and the others were all put to death.
units.literal: Shouwen had a beloved concubine trapped in the rebel city who was taken by Sizhan; when the city was recovered, Congyi obtained all of Sizhan's maids and servants; Shouwen asked for his beloved concubine; though Congyi gave her to him, in his mind he was not satisfied, so he exposed the former crime, secretly reported to Guo Wei, and requested that Shouwen be removed—he and Wang Yi and the others were all put to death.

units.zh: 戊辰，永興軍節度使兼兵馬都部署郭從義加同平章事，徙華州節度使。
units.en: On wuchen, the Yongxing military governor and concurrent commander of army and horse Guo Congyi was given the additional title of Grand Councilor and transferred to military governor of Hua.
units.literal: On wuchen, the Yongxing military governor and concurrent commander of army and horse Guo Congyi was given the additional title of Grand Councilor and transferred to military governor of Hua.

units.zh: 至九日夕，有部曲曹彥進告，思綰欲於十一日夜與同惡五百人奔南山入蜀。
units.en: By the evening of the ninth a subordinate, Cao Yanjin, reported that Sizhan intended on the night of the eleventh, with five hundred fellow villains, to flee south into the mountains and enter Shu.
units.literal: By the evening of the ninth, a subordinate, Cao Yanjin, reported that Sizhan intended on the night of the eleventh, with five hundred fellow villains, to flee south into the mountains and enter Shu.

units.zh: 是日詰旦，再促上路，雲俟夜進途。
units.en: At dawn that day he was again urged to take the road; he said he would wait for night to set out.
units.literal: At dawn that day he was again urged to take the road; he said he would wait for night to advance on the journey.

units.zh: 臣尋與王峻入城，分兵守四門，其趙思綰部下軍，各已執帶，遂至牙署，令趙思綰至則執之，與一行徒黨，並處置訖。」
units.en: Your servant then entered the city with Wang Jun and divided troops to guard the four gates. Sizhan's subordinate troops had all already belted on their arms. We then reached the headquarters office, seized Zhao Sizhan when he arrived, and dealt with him and his whole party of followers."
